rules.title: Eviction for criminal convictions and related conduct
rules.requirement: A landlord may file for eviction if the tenant or a person permitted by the tenant has been convicted of certain crimes including drug offenses, theft, or human trafficking related to the premises. No eviction suit may be brought more than two years after the conviction or related event.
rules.summary_plain: You can be evicted if you or someone you allow to live with you has been convicted of certain crimes related to the property, but eviction must be filed within two years of the conviction or release.
rules.summary_plain_es: Puede ser desalojado si usted o alguien que permite vivir con usted ha sido condenado por ciertos delitos relacionados con la propiedad, pero el desalojo debe presentarse dentro de los dos años posteriores a la condena o liberación.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to tenants convicted of drug offenses, theft, or human trafficking related to the premises or allowing such persons to reside there.
rules.exemptions_text: Does not apply to tenants allowing juveniles found delinquent for drug use or possession to reside at the property.
rules.quoted_span: No eviction suit may be brought more than two years after : the juvenile was found to be delinquent; conviction of the person; or after the person’s release fr om incarceration, whichever is later. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(p)).

rules.title: Eviction from owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings
rules.requirement: Tenants in owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can only be evicted for specific causes such as lease expiration, nonpayment of rent, disorderly conduct, property damage, or lease violations, with required notice periods depending on tenancy type.
rules.key_value: 1 to 3 months notice depending on tenancy
rules.summary_plain: If you rent in an owner-occupied two- or three-family home, you can only be evicted for certain reasons and with proper notice, which varies by your lease type.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si alquila en una casa de dos o tres familias ocupada por el propietario, solo puede ser desalojado por ciertas razones y con el aviso adecuado, que varía según su tipo de contrato.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to tenants in owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings.
rules.quoted_span: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only when a court issues an order for eviction. However, in these cases, the landlord must prove that the tenant (a) is staying after the expiration of the term of the lease, (b) is staying after a failure to pay rent, (c) is disorderly so as to destroy the peace and quiet of other tenants, (d) willfully destroys or damages the premises, (e) constantly violates the written rules and regulations or (f) violates any lease provision where the lease reserves a right of re-entry for such violations.

rules.title: Eviction procedures for rooming and boarding houses
rules.requirement: Owners of rooming and boarding houses must follow good cause and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, including giving at least three working days’ notice to the County Welfare Board before starting eviction.
rules.key_value: 3 working days notice to County Welfare Board
rules.summary_plain: If you live in a rooming or boarding house, the owner must have good cause to evict you and must notify the County Welfare Board at least three working days before starting eviction.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si vive en una casa de habitaciones o pensión, el propietario debe tener una causa justificada para desalojarlo y debe notificar a la Junta de Bienestar del Condado al menos tres días hábiles antes de iniciar el desalojo.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to residents of rooming and boarding houses as defined by state law.
rules.exemptions_text: Certain exceptions apply such as hotels with mostly temporary occupancy, dormitories, and residences for the disabled.
rules.quoted_span: The Regulations Governing Rooming and Boarding Houses...require owners of rooming and boarding houses to follow the good causes and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents...owner give at least three (3) working days’ notice to the County Welfare Board before starting the eviction action for any resident (N.J.A.C. 5:26-3.4(c)).

rules.title: Eviction procedures for public housing tenants
rules.requirement: Public housing authorities must follow state eviction laws and HUD regulations. A tenant may request a hearing after receiving a termination notice, and eviction cannot begin until the hearing decision is delivered and a notice to vacate served.
rules.summary_plain: If you live in public housing, you have the right to a hearing before eviction, and the housing authority must follow state and federal rules.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si vive en vivienda pública, tiene derecho a una audiencia antes del desalojo, y la autoridad de vivienda debe seguir las normas estatales y federales.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to tenants in public housing authorities.
rules.quoted_span: Public housing authorities must follow State laws regarding evictions as well as the regulations of the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1; 24 C.F.R. 966 et seq. ). In the case of an eviction, a public housing tenant may request a hearing from the housing authority after receiving a notice of termination of tenancy.

rules.title: Landlord occupancy and demolition eviction penalties
rules.requirement: If a landlord gives notice to personally occupy a unit, they must occupy it for at least six months or be liable for three times damages plus attorney fees. If the landlord gives notice to demolish or retire the property from residential use, they must not use it residentially for five years or face triple damages, civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation, and registration restrictions.
rules.key_value: 6 months occupancy; 5 years no residential use
rules.summary_plain: If your landlord evicts you to live in or demolish the unit, they must follow strict rules or pay you damages and penalties.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si su propietario lo desaloja para vivir en la unidad o demolerla, debe seguir reglas estrictas o pagarle daños y sanciones.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies when landlord gives eviction notice for personal occupancy or demolition/retirement from residential use.
rules.penalty: Three times damages plus attorney fees; civil penalty up to $10,000 per violation
rules.quoted_span: When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the landlord wishes to personally occupy the unit the landlord must occupy the unit for at least six (6) months...When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the landlord seeks to permanently board up or demolish the building...the landlord must not use this property for residential use for a period of five (5) years...the landlord...may be liable for a civil penalty up to $10,000.00 for each violation of this law.

rules.title: Prohibition on landlord reprisal evictions
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot evict, substantially alter lease terms, or refuse to renew a lease in retaliation for a tenant exercising certain civil rights such as enforcing lease or law rights, making good faith complaints, or organizing tenants.
rules.summary_plain: Your landlord cannot evict or punish you for asserting your rights or reporting problems in good faith.
rules.summary_plain_es: Su propietario no puede desalojarlo ni castigarlo por hacer valer sus derechos o reportar problemas de buena fe.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to all rental properties except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions_text: Excludes owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-10.10). The law against reprisal applies to all rental properties used for dwelling purposes, including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.

rules.title: Foreclosure tenant protections and notice requirements
rules.requirement: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction. A buyer who wants to personally occupy a foreclosed property must give tenants a 90-day notice to quit. New owners must notify tenants of ownership change within 10 business days in English and Spanish, with specific notice posting requirements depending on building size.
rules.key_value: 90-day notice to quit; 10 business days notice of ownership change
rules.summary_plain: If your home is foreclosed, you cannot be evicted just because of foreclosure. New owners must notify you quickly and give 90 days’ notice if they want to live there.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si su casa es embargada, no pueden desalojarlo solo por la ejecución hipotecaria. Los nuevos propietarios deben notificarle rápidamente y darle un aviso de 90 días si quieren vivir allí.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to tenants in foreclosed residential properties.
rules.exemptions_text: Month-to-month tenants and owner-occupied two- and three-family units are not exempt from the 90-day notice requirement.
rules.quoted_span: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction in New Jersey...Before a tenant can be evicted due to foreclosure, the landlord must provide the tenant with a 90 -day notice to qui t...Any person acquiring a foreclosed property containing one or more residential rental units must provide notices to the tenants in English and Spanish, within 10 business days after the sale...
